name: Muhammad Moosa Raza
affiliation: M.Sc. Ecology & Nature Management, RUDN University
tagline: Remote sensing for floods, drought and land-system change — with a working obsession for when these methods quietly fail

availability.detail: Open to positions in remote sensing, hydrology, land-system science and climate risk. Happy to discuss how my work could extend a group's existing research.

about: I build satellite-based environmental measurements, and then I try to break them. Across nine open studies over Pakistan, the recurring result is that the standard way of applying a method returns a confident number that does not survive scrutiny: a drought index flagging 118 months of extreme drought when 112 were near-normal, a post-flood vegetation signal that turns out to be ordinary crop phenology, an Earth Engine distance operator failing silently and quietly costing model skill.

That thread now defines how I work. I validate chronologically rather than randomly so a model cannot memorise the events it is judged on, cross-check findings against a physically unrelated sensor, and publish the negative and the uncertain next to the headline result. Every study ships with its code, training data and a written account of what it cannot support.

I am looking for a PhD where this becomes the research question rather than a habit: how we establish that an Earth observation measurement is trustworthy before it informs a flood warning, a drought declaration or a carbon budget.

researchInterests.title: Measurement validity in Earth observation
researchInterests.description: Silent failure modes in operational EO workflows — validation designs that leak, indices undefined over the regimes where they are most needed, and cloud or orbit sampling that biases a result without ever raising an error.

researchInterests.title: Floods and hydrological extremes
researchInterests.description: SAR-based inundation mapping and event-based flood susceptibility, including how compositing windows and relative-orbit choices distort estimates of flood extent.

researchInterests.title: Drought and agricultural water in semi-arid systems
researchInterests.description: Drought indices and soil moisture retrieval where irrigation, zero-inflated rainfall and closed canopies break the assumptions the standard methods are built on.

researchInterests.title: Land-system change and ecosystem carbon
researchInterests.description: Multi-decadal land cover dynamics and the carbon consequences of rapid urban expansion, linking land transitions to measurable ecosystem service loss.

approach.title: Validate against time, not at random
approach.description: Chronological, event-based holdout so a model never sees the events it is scored on. Random splits let pixels from one flood land in both train and test, which inflates the scores everyone reports.

approach.title: Cross-check with an unrelated sensor
approach.description: A radar result checked against an optical one, or a retrieval against reanalysis and rain gauges. Agreement between physically independent measurements is worth more than a high score from one.

approach.title: Report the number that does not flatter
approach.description: District-mean NDVI anomaly of −0.005 would have implied no flood impact at all. The write-up leads with that, then shows why the map still holds, rather than quoting the reassuring figure.

approach.title: Ship the code and the caveats
approach.description: Every study is public: code, training data, GIS exports and a model card stating the limits. If a result depends on a threshold or a product choice, that dependency is documented, not buried.

bullets: Designed and published nine end-to-end EO studies over Pakistan covering flood mapping, flood susceptibility, drought, soil moisture, speckle filtering and crop mapping
Established a consistent methodological standard across all of them: chronological validation, independent cross-sensor checks, and explicit reporting of negative and null results

Identified and documented several failure modes in widely used workflows, including a silent Google Earth Engine distance-operator fault and a 95% false-alarm rate in textbook SPI over zero-inflated rainfall
Released every study as open code with training data, GIS exports and written limitations, so results can be reproduced and contested

experience.role: Master’s Thesis Researcher — Remote Sensing & Carbon Modelling
bullets: Designed a multi-decadal (1993–2023) LULC analysis pipeline using Landsat imagery in Google Earth Engine
Implemented Random Forest classification reaching 97.8%–99.2% accuracy, Kappa 0.971–0.989
Quantified urban expansion (+117%) and vegetation loss (−27,639 ha) across Lahore District
Estimated ecosystem carbon dynamics: a total loss of roughly 3.15 million metric tons
Integrated the InVEST carbon model as an independent check on the class-based estimate
Key contribution: showed how urban land transitions drive large-scale carbon loss in rapidly developing regions

Modelling & Analysis: Accuracy assessment (confusion matrix, Kappa, IoU, ROC)
